title: Correct friction coefficient
description: Essential Criteria: Student must calculate μ = 0.5 from the first scenario using equilibrium conditions.

title: Correct final friction force
description: Essential Criteria: Student must determine the friction force is 20 N in the second scenario, recognizing it equals the horizontal component.

title: First scenario equilibrium analysis
description: Important Criteria: Student must apply Newton's first law to both horizontal (F = friction) and vertical (N = mg) directions for constant velocity.

title: Second scenario normal force
description: Important Criteria: Student must correctly calculate the new normal force including the vertical component of the applied force (N = mg + Fsinθ).

title: Force component decomposition
description: Important Criteria: Student must resolve the angled force into horizontal (Fcosθ) and vertical (Fsinθ) components using given trigonometric values.

title: Static vs kinetic friction check
description: Important Criteria: Student must compare the required friction (Fcosθ) to maximum static friction to confirm motion type.

title: Units in final answers
description: Optional Criteria: Student should include proper units (no units for μ, N for force) in final answers.

title: Using wrong friction type
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if student uses kinetic friction formula without checking if horizontal force exceeds maximum static friction.

title: Sign error in normal force
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if student subtracts the vertical force component when calculating normal force (N = mg - Fsinθ).
